 feature 16/11/2026 Arabian Gulf Cup champions are looking to build on last week's superb win against South Korea With the postponement of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup until later in 2027, this international window has taken on a very different context for many teams across Asia - and Saudi Arabia is one of those.
 Rather than using it as vital preparation ahead of a tournament on home soil, the added time has given manager Georgios Donis a chance to broaden the net. 
 Seeking to build on the national team’s superb success at the Arabian Gulf Cup last month, the former Al Hilal, Al Wehda and Al Khaleej coach can now look at different options as he tries to find the right formula to help the Green Falcons continue on their upward trajectory.
 After last week’s impressive 3-2 win against South Korea in Qatar on Friday, we run the rule over some names to keep an eye on ahead of Tuesday’s clash with Uzbekistan.
 Saudi Arabia manager Georgios Donis puts his side through their paces on the training pitch -------- 
 Marwan Al Sahafi 
 The exciting winger has been part of the national team set-up for a number of years but has yet to nail down a berth in the starting XI. And that’s after a few seasons in Europe, first with Beerschot and then with Royal Antwerp.
 Now back at parent club Al Ittihad, the arrival of manager Jens Wissing has given the 22-year-old a chance for a fresh start, and after scoring his first international goal against South Korea, Al Sahafi now has goals in back-to-back games given he also netted in the recent AFC Champions League Elite fixture against Al Ain.
 Is this the boost the forward needs to deliver on his promise?
 Marwan Al Sahafi is back at Al Ittihad and performing in the RSL -------- 
 Sultan Tunker 
 The selection of the 28-year-old Al Hazem defender was a bold choice by Donis, and one that came very much from left-field.
 Uncapped before the South Korea game, the late-bloomer has been a solid presence in the heart of defence for the Roshn Saudi League side this season, with a 62 percent success rate in duels, 18 interceptions and 60 clearances, as well as 13 blocked shots.
 The question Donis will want answered is whether Tankar can translate his domestic form into the international arena, with the step up in intensity and quality that comes with that. His selection, however, does show he is very much in the calculations.
 Sultan Tunker has been rewarded for his form at Al Hazem with a place in the Saudi Arabia side -------- 
 Abdulmalik Al Oyayari 
 Once regarded as one of the RSL’s most exciting young talents, the 22-year-old finally made his international debut off the bench against South Korea having previously been called up under Herve Renard.
 Capable of playing right-back or in midfield, that versatility could be useful as Al Oyayari boasts value in multiple areas of the pitch.
 With NEOM Sports Club enjoying a better campaign than in their RSL debut, he has made himself a regular in Christophe Galtier’s team. 
 Consequentially, that regular football has Al Oyayari back in the frame at international level.
 NEOM SC's versatile star Abdulmalik Al Oyayari -------- 
 Mohammed Abu Al Shamat 
 The 24-year-old has the strongest domestic form of any player on this list, the flying full-back starring for Al Qadsiah as they push themselves into title contention .
 Abu Al Shamat’s four goals and four assists in the 2026-27 RSL make him one of the most threatening - and productive - players in the competition, although it’d be accurate to say he’s never quite managed to translate that to the international scene.
 That is now his challenge: to cement a place in Donis’ starting XI and deliver the same level of output he has for Brendan Rodgers’ hugely ambitious side .
 Al Qadsiah's Mohammed Abu Al Shamat features for Saudi Arabia against South Korea -------- 
 Hamed Al Shanqiti 
 Al Kholood are earning a reputation for giving emerging young talent an opportunity - and goalkeeper Hamed Al Shanqiti is another name that can be added to that list.
 The 21-year-old shot-stopper was handed the gloves this season after joining on loan from Al Ittihad and was a key factor in Al Kholood’s fast start to this season , earning the Young Player of the Month award for August .
 The question now is whether Al Shanqiti’s form and potential between the sticks is compelling enough to displace long-time regular Mohammed Al Owais?
 With still 12 months until the Asian Cup, he is perhaps one that might benefit from its postponement.
